title: LLM-Eraser: Optimizing Large Language Model Unlearning through Selective Pruning

problem.claim: Unlearning unwanted knowledge from autoregressive LLMs requires removing undesirable information while preserving desirable knowledge.

gap.claim: Gradient-ascent approaches over undesired knowledge can compromise performance on desired knowledge.

contributions.claim: LLM-Eraser is a two-stage approach that selectively identifies and edits parameters associated with undesirable knowledge.
The localization stage uses neuron scores and trainable soft masks to identify parameters crucial to undesired knowledge.
The unlearning stage prunes identified parameters and applies selective post-training to enhance selectiveness.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe LLM-Eraser as a novel two-stage approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across five task datasets, the authors report near-random multiple-choice performance on erased knowledge and an average performance deficit of only 2.5% on desirable knowledge.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work targets unlearning unwanted knowledge while preserving desirable knowledge in autoregressive LLMs.
Prior gradient-ascent approaches may damage performance on desired knowledge.
LLM-Eraser localizes parameters linked to undesirable knowledge and then unlearns by pruning and selective post-training.
Experiments across five task datasets report effective erasure with a 2.5% average performance deficit.

source_observation.claim: The method separates parameter localization from parameter pruning and selective post-training.

interpretation.claim: Separating identification from editing may support more targeted unlearning than directly optimizing the full model.

application.claim: Unlearning systems may benefit from first identifying parameters associated with the target knowledge before editing them.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this separation generalizes beyond the reported task datasets or model settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated models, datasets, baselines, or detailed experimental protocol.
The abstract does not report localization accuracy, pruning scale, or post-training configuration.
The abstract does not provide evidence about privacy guarantees, harmfulness reduction beyond the reported tasks, or long-term retention of erased knowledge.
